items.statement: Exercise strict control over labeling issued for use in drug product labeling operations.
items.quote: Strict control shall be exercised over labeling issued for use in drug product labeling operations.

items.statement: Carefully examine labeling materials issued for a batch for identity and for conformity to the labeling specified in the master or batch production records.
items.quote: Labeling materials issued for a batch shall be carefully examined for identity and conformity to the labeling specified in the master or batch production records.

items.statement: Use procedures to reconcile the quantities of labeling issued, used and returned.
items.quote: Procedures shall be used to reconcile the quantities of labeling issued, used, and returned

items.statement: Labeling reconciliation procedures require evaluation of discrepancies between the quantity of drug product finished and the quantity of labeling issued when the discrepancies fall outside narrow preset limits based on historical operating data.
items.quote: shall require evaluation of discrepancies found between the quantity of drug product finished and the quantity of labeling issued when such discrepancies are outside narrow preset limits based on historical operating data

items.statement: Investigate labeling reconciliation discrepancies that fall outside the narrow preset limits through the formal investigation process for unexplained discrepancies and batch failures.
items.quote: Such discrepancies shall be investigated in accordance with § 211.192.

items.statement: Labeling reconciliation may be omitted for cut or roll labeling only if a 100-percent examination for correct labeling is performed.
items.quote: Labeling reconciliation is waived for cut or roll labeling if a 100-percent examination for correct labeling is performed in accordance with § 211.122(g)(2).
items.condition: cut or roll labeling with 100-percent examination

items.statement: Destroy all excess labeling that bears lot or control numbers.
items.quote: All excess labeling bearing lot or control numbers shall be destroyed.
items.condition: excess labeling bears lot or control numbers

items.statement: Maintain and store returned labeling in a way that prevents mixups and provides proper identification.
items.quote: Returned labeling shall be maintained and stored in a manner to prevent mixups and provide proper identification.

items.statement: Have written procedures describing in sufficient detail the controls used for issuing labeling, and follow them.
items.quote: Procedures shall be written describing in sufficient detail the control procedures employed for the issuance of labeling; such written procedures shall be followed.

items.statement: Have written procedures designed to assure that correct labels, labeling and packaging materials are used for drug products, follow them, and include in them the required packaging and labeling control features.
items.quote: There shall be written procedures designed to assure that correct labels, labeling, and packaging materials are used for drug products; such written procedures shall be followed. These procedures shall incorporate the following features:

items.statement: Written packaging and labeling procedures, designed to assure correct labels, labeling and packaging materials are used, include prevention of mixups and cross-contamination by physical or spatial separation from operations on other drug products.
items.quote: Prevention of mixups and cross-contamination by physical or spatial separation from operations on other drug products.

items.statement: Written packaging and labeling procedures, designed to assure correct labels, labeling and packaging materials are used, include identification and handling of filled containers set aside unlabeled for later labeling, to preclude mislabeling of containers, lots or part lots; identification need not be on each container but must be enough to determine name, strength, quantity of contents and lot or control number of each container.
items.quote: Identification and handling of filled drug product containers that are set aside and held in unlabeled condition for future labeling operations to preclude mislabeling of individual containers, lots, or portions of lots. Identification need not be applied to each individual container but shall be sufficient to determine name, strength, quantity of contents, and lot or control number of each container.
items.condition: filled containers held unlabeled for future labeling

items.statement: Written packaging and labeling procedures, designed to assure correct labels, labeling and packaging materials are used, include identification of the drug product with a lot or control number that allows the manufacturing and control history of the batch to be determined.
items.quote: Identification of the drug product with a lot or control number that permits determination of the history of the manufacture and control of the batch.

items.statement: Written packaging and labeling procedures, designed to assure correct labels, labeling and packaging materials are used, include examination of packaging and labeling materials for suitability and correctness before packaging operations, with the examination documented in the batch production record.
items.quote: Examination of packaging and labeling materials for suitability and correctness before packaging operations, and documentation of such examination in the batch production record.

items.statement: Written packaging and labeling procedures, designed to assure correct labels, labeling and packaging materials are used, include inspection of packaging and labeling facilities immediately before use to assure all drug products from previous operations have been removed.
items.quote: Inspection of the packaging and labeling facilities immediately before use to assure that all drug products have been removed from previous operations.

items.statement: Written packaging and labeling procedures, designed to assure correct labels, labeling and packaging materials are used, include inspection of packaging and labeling facilities immediately before use to assure that packaging and labeling materials unsuitable for the next operations have been removed.
items.quote: Inspection shall also be made to assure that packaging and labeling materials not suitable for subsequent operations have been removed.

items.statement: Written packaging and labeling procedures, designed to assure correct labels, labeling and packaging materials are used, include documentation of the results of the pre-use packaging and labeling facility inspections in the batch production records.
items.quote: Results of inspection shall be documented in the batch production records.

items.statement: Package each OTC drug product (except dermatological, dentifrice, insulin or lozenge products) for retail sale in a tamper-evident package if the product is accessible to the public while held for sale.
items.quote: Each manufacturer and packer who packages an OTC drug product (except a dermatological, dentifrice, insulin, or lozenge product) for retail sale shall package the product in a tamper-evident package, if this product is accessible to the public while held for sale.
items.condition: OTC product for retail sale accessible to public

items.statement: Make the tamper-evident package for OTC retail drug products (except dermatological, dentifrice, insulin or lozenge products) distinctive by design, or use one or more indicators or barriers to entry with an identifying characteristic such as a pattern, name, registered trademark, logo or picture.
items.quote: To reduce the likelihood of successful tampering and to increase the likelihood that consumers will discover if a product has been tampered with, the package is required to be distinctive by design or by the use of one or more indicators or barriers to entry that employ an identifying characteristic (e.g., a pattern, name, registered trademark, logo, or picture).

items.statement: Design the tamper-evident feature of OTC retail drug product packages (except dermatological, dentifrice, insulin or lozenge products) so that it remains intact when handled reasonably during manufacture, distribution and retail display, and confirm it does.
items.quote: The tamper-evident feature shall be designed to and shall remain intact when handled in a reasonable manner during manufacture, distribution, and retail display.

items.statement: In addition to the tamper-evident package, seal any two-piece hard gelatin capsule sold OTC at retail (except dermatological, dentifrice, insulin or lozenge products) using an acceptable tamper-evident technology.
items.quote: In addition to the tamper-evident packaging feature described in paragraph (b)(1) of this section, any two-piece, hard gelatin capsule covered by this section must be sealed using an acceptable tamper-evident technology.
items.condition: two-piece hard gelatin capsule OTC retail

items.statement: Each retail package of an OTC drug product covered by the tamper-evident packaging rule (except ammonia inhalant in crushable glass ampules, or aerosol products that depend on a liquefied or compressed gas to expel the contents) bears a statement alerting consumers to the specific tamper-evident feature(s) used.
items.quote: In order to alert consumers to the specific tamper-evident feature(s) used, each retail package of an OTC drug product covered by this section (except ammonia inhalant in crushable glass ampules or aerosol products that depend upon the power of a liquefied or compressed gas to expel the contents from the container) is required to bear a statement that:

items.statement: Each retail package of an OTC drug product covered by the tamper-evident packaging rule (except ammonia inhalant in crushable glass ampules, or aerosol products that depend on a liquefied or compressed gas to expel the contents) bears a statement alerting consumers to the tamper-evident feature(s) used, and that statement identifies all tamper-evident features and any capsule sealing technologies used.
items.quote: Identifies all tamper-evident feature(s) and any capsule sealing technologies used to comply with paragraph (b) of this section;

items.statement: Each retail package of an OTC drug product covered by the tamper-evident packaging rule (except ammonia inhalant in crushable glass ampules, or aerosol products that depend on a liquefied or compressed gas to expel the contents) bears a statement alerting consumers to the tamper-evident feature(s) used, and that statement is placed prominently on the package.
items.quote: Is prominently placed on the package; and

items.statement: Each retail package of an OTC drug product covered by the tamper-evident packaging rule (except ammonia inhalant in crushable glass ampules, or aerosol products that depend on a liquefied or compressed gas to expel the contents) bears a statement alerting consumers to the tamper-evident feature(s) used, and that statement is placed so that it is unaffected if the tamper-evident feature is breached or missing.
items.quote: Is so placed that it will be unaffected if the tamper-evident feature of the package is breached or missing.

items.statement: If the tamper-evident feature chosen for an OTC retail drug product uses an identifying characteristic, refer to that characteristic in the labeling statement.
items.quote: If the tamper-evident feature chosen to meet the requirements in paragraph (b) of this section uses an identifying characteristic, that characteristic is required to be referred to in the labeling statement.

items.statement: A manufacturer or packer may request an exemption from the tamper-evident packaging and labeling requirements.
items.quote: A manufacturer or packer may request an exemption from the packaging and labeling requirements of this section.

items.statement: Submit any request for exemption from the tamper-evident packaging and labeling requirements as a citizen petition to FDA.
items.quote: A request for an exemption is required to be submitted in the form of a citizen petition under § 10.30 of this chapter

items.statement: Clearly mark the envelope of a tamper-evident exemption petition as a request for exemption from the tamper-evident packaging rule.
items.quote: should be clearly identified on the envelope as a “Request for Exemption from the Tamper-Evident Packaging Rule.”

items.statement: An exemption petition from the tamper-evident packaging and labeling requirements contains the name of the drug product, or for a drug class, the class name and a list of products in that class.
items.quote: The name of the drug product or, if the petition seeks an exemption for a drug class, the name of the drug class, and a list of products within that class.

items.statement: An exemption petition from the tamper-evident packaging and labeling requirements contains the reasons why the product's compliance with those requirements is unnecessary or cannot be achieved.
items.quote: The reasons that the drug product's compliance with the tamper-evident packaging or labeling requirements of this section is unnecessary or cannot be achieved.

items.statement: An exemption petition from the tamper-evident packaging and labeling requirements describes alternative steps available, or already taken by the petitioner, to reduce the likelihood of malicious adulteration of the product or drug class.
items.quote: A description of alternative steps that are available, or that the petitioner has already taken, to reduce the likelihood that the product or drug class will be the subject of malicious adulteration.

items.statement: An exemption petition from the tamper-evident packaging and labeling requirements contains any other information justifying the exemption.
items.quote: Other information justifying an exemption.

items.statement: Holders of approved new drug applications for OTC drug products notify FDA of packaging and labeling changes made to comply with the tamper-evident requirements, through the supplement and change-reporting process.
items.quote: Holders of approved new drug applications for OTC drug products are required under § 314.70 of this chapter to provide the agency with notification of changes in packaging and labeling to comply with the requirements of this section.
items.condition: holder of approved NDA for OTC product

items.statement: Packaging and labeling changes required by the tamper-evident rule may be implemented before FDA approval, as allowed by the change-reporting rules for approved applications.
items.quote: Changes in packaging and labeling required by this regulation may be made before FDA approval, as provided under § 314.70(c) of this chapter.
items.condition: holder of approved NDA for OTC product

items.statement: Obtain prior FDA approval before making manufacturing changes by which capsules are to be sealed under an approved new drug application for an OTC product.
items.quote: Manufacturing changes by which capsules are to be sealed require prior FDA approval under § 314.70(b) of this chapter.
items.condition: holder of approved NDA; capsule sealing change

items.statement: Examine packaged and labeled products during finishing operations to assure that containers and packages in the lot carry the correct label.
items.quote: Packaged and labeled products shall be examined during finishing operations to provide assurance that containers and packages in the lot have the correct label.

items.statement: Collect a representative sample of units at the completion of finishing operations and visually examine them for correct labeling.
items.quote: A representative sample of units shall be collected at the completion of finishing operations and shall be visually examined for correct labeling.

items.statement: Record the results of the in-process label examinations and the end-of-finishing visual sample examination in the batch production or control records.
items.quote: Results of these examinations shall be recorded in the batch production or control records.

items.statement: Give each drug product an expiration date, determined by appropriate stability testing, to assure it meets applicable standards of identity, strength, quality and purity at the time of use.
items.quote: To assure that a drug product meets applicable standards of identity, strength, quality, and purity at the time of use, it shall bear an expiration date determined by appropriate stability testing described in § 211.166.

items.statement: Relate expiration dates to any storage conditions stated on the labeling, as determined by stability studies.
items.quote: Expiration dates shall be related to any storage conditions stated on the labeling, as determined by stability studies described in § 211.166.

items.statement: If a drug product is to be reconstituted at the time of dispensing, include expiration information on its labeling for both the reconstituted and unreconstituted product.
items.quote: If the drug product is to be reconstituted at the time of dispensing, its labeling shall bear expiration information for both the reconstituted and unreconstituted drug products.

items.statement: Show expiration dates on labeling in line with FDA's labeling requirements for expiration dates.
items.quote: Expiration dates shall appear on labeling in accordance with the requirements of § 201.17 of this chapter.

items.statement: Investigational new drug products may be exempt from expiration dating only if stability studies during their clinical use demonstrate they meet appropriate standards or specifications.
items.quote: New drug products for investigational use are exempt from the requirements of this section, provided that they meet appropriate standards or specifications as demonstrated by stability studies during their use in clinical investigations.

items.statement: Where investigational new drug products are to be reconstituted at the time of dispensing, include expiration information for the reconstituted product on their labeling.
items.quote: Where new drug products for investigational use are to be reconstituted at the time of dispensing, their labeling shall bear expiration information for the reconstituted drug product.

(f) Allergenic extracts that are labeled “No U.S. Standard of Potency” are exempt
